title: The body, feeling ill, and seeing a doctor
goal: Name parts of the body, describe symptoms, and talk at a pharmacy or health center using the right speech level.
bekal: parts of the body and their two speech levels
asking after a sick person, and answering

dialogs.title: Paguneman — At the pharmacy
dialogs.intro: Rani wakes up with a heavy head and a sore throat. Sari takes her to the pharmacy at the end of the alley.

lines.speaker: Apotéker:
lines.text: Wilujeng énjing. Aya nu tiasa dibantosan?
lines.id: Good morning. How can I help?
lines.literal: good morning. is-there what can be-helped?

lines.speaker: Rani:
lines.text: Punten, abdi teu damang ti kamari.
lines.id: Excuse me, I haven't been feeling well since yesterday.
lines.literal: excuse-me, I not well since yesterday.

lines.speaker: Rani:
lines.text: Sirah nyeri, tikoro ogé nyeri upami neureuy.
lines.id: My head hurts, and my throat hurts when I swallow.
lines.literal: head hurt, throat also hurt if swallow.

lines.speaker: Apotéker:
lines.id: Do you feel hot? A fever?

lines.speaker: Rani:
lines.text: Wengi tadi muriang. Ayeuna mah ngan lieur.
lines.id: I had a fever last night. Now I'm just dizzy.
lines.literal: night past fever. now [mah] only dizzy.

lines.speaker: Rani:
lines.id: Nothing yet. I was afraid of taking the wrong thing.

lines.speaker: Apotéker:
lines.text: Saé. Ieu kanggo tikoro, diseuseup tilu kali sadinten.
lines.id: Good. This is for your throat, suck one three times a day.
lines.literal: good. this for throat, be-sucked three times a-day.

lines.speaker: Apotéker:
lines.text: Ieu, saatos tuang. Ulah dina beuteung kosong.
lines.id: This one, after eating. Not on an empty stomach.
lines.literal: this, after eat. don't in stomach empty.

lines.speaker: Rani:
lines.text: Upami tilu dinten teu cageur, kumaha?
lines.id: What if I'm not better in three days?
lines.literal: if three day not recover, how?

lines.speaker: Apotéker:
lines.text: Kedah ka dokter. Puskésmas caket, hareupeun pasar.
lines.id: Then see a doctor. The health center is close, opposite the market.
lines.literal: must to doctor. health-center near, at front market.

lines.speaker: Rani:
lines.id: Thank you very much. How much is it all together?

notes: **Teu damang** = not well, under the weather (lemes). It's the most polite way to say you're ill. The loma form is **gering**. ⚠️ For someone you respect, use **udur**: *Ibu nuju udur* = Mother is ill.
**Nyeri** = hurting, a pain in part of the body. Compare *gering*, being ill as a state. *Sirah nyeri* = my head hurts; *kuring gering* = I'm ill.
**Muriang** = fever, feverish. Indonesian has the same word (*meriang*), so if you know some Indonesian, it's an easy one.
**Lieur** = dizzy, a headache. ⚠️ Say it as two beats, *lee-EUR*. It's also used for being confused: *lieur mikiranana* = it makes my head spin just thinking about it.
**Neureuy** = to swallow. One of those double-*eu* words worth practicing: *neu-REUY*.

**Cageur** = recovered, healthy. It's part of a famous Sundanese saying: **cageur, bageur, bener, pinter, singer**: healthy, kind, honest, clever, skillful, the five qualities hoped for in a good Sundanese person.

grammars.title: Describing symptoms
body: A Sundanese complaint is very simple: **body part + how it feels**, with no verb at all.
after: To make clear whose head it is, add a pronoun: *Sirah abdi nyeri*. But plain *Sirah nyeri* is more natural: context tells you whose it is.

Some complaints have their own verbs: **utah** (to vomit), **budah** (diarrhea), **batuk** (cough), **beuki** (a cold; the same word also means "more and more," and context tells them apart), **teu tuang** (no appetite), **teu tiasa kulem** (can't sleep).

⚠️ When asking someone else, use the respectful lemes forms: *Naon nu karaos?* (what are you feeling), *Tos dipariksa?* (have you been examined), *Tos ngaleueut obat?* (have you taken medicine). Asking *tos nginum obat?* sounds too casual for someone who's ill.

blocks.text: ⚠️ Notice **leungeun** (hand) and **panangan** (hand, lemes). The polite *panangan* also turns up in courteous phrases: *punten, panangan abdi kotor* = sorry, my hands are dirty. For feet, the lemes form is **sampéan**, which in Javanese means "you," so don't mix them up.

sections.title: At the doctor's and the pharmacy

blocks.title: What the patient says
items: **Abdi teu damang ti kamari.** — I've been ill since yesterday.
**Sirah nyeri sareng muriang.** — I have a headache and a fever.
**Tos tilu dinten kieu.** — It's been like this for three days.
**Teu acan ngaleueut obat.** — I haven't taken any medicine yet.
**Kedah dipariksa henteu?** — Do I need to be examined?
**Obatna diseuseup sabaraha kali sadinten?** — How many times a day do I take it?
**Aya efék sampingna teu?** — Are there any side effects?

head: What you'll hear
Meaning
rows: How long has it been like this?
Please sit down, let's take a look.
Three times a day, after meals.
You need rest, no work for now.
*Upami teu cageur, wangsul deui ka dieu.*
If you don't get better, come back here.

blocks.text: **Mugia énggal damang** is the standard way to say "get well soon," and you'll hear it from almost everyone who knows you're ill. Just answer *aamiin, hatur nuhun*. The loma form: *muga-muga geura cageur*.

blocks.title: Visiting someone who's ill
items: **Kumaha damang, Bu?** — How are you feeling, ma'am?
**Tos tiasa tuang?** — Can you eat yet?
**Ulah seueur teuing ngalih.** — Don't move around too much.
**Upami peryogi naon-naon, wartosan waé.** — If you need anything, just let me know.

exercises.prompt: Give the Sundanese for these parts of the body (loma form).

items: My throat hurts when I swallow. → ____
I haven't taken any medicine yet.
It's been like this for three days.
How many times a day do I take it?
You need rest, no work for now.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order.

answers: hulu/sirah — panon — ceuli — beuteung — leungeun — suku
Sirah nyeri. — Beuteung nyeri. — Awak panas. — Huntu nyeri. — Tikoro nyeri upami neureuy. — Sukuna bareuh.
Abdi teu damang ti kamari. — Teu acan ngaleueut obat. — Tos tilu dinten kieu. — Obatna diseuseup sabaraha kali sadinten? — Mugia énggal damang, Bu. — Kedah ngaso, ulah damel heula.
Abdi teu damang ti kamari. — Nu karaos naon? — Teu acan ngaleueut obat. — Mugia énggal damang. — Ieu saatos tuang.
